claims.text: Deep-learning-based simulations could overcome current limitations in determining high-temperature solid and liquid properties of multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
The proposed intervention is the use of machine-learning simulations, specifically deep-learning models.
The intervention applies to multicomponent high-entropy alloys in high-temperature solid and liquid states.
Configurational entropy is a structural mediator of the proposed intervention's effect.
Lattice distortion is a structural mediator of the proposed intervention's effect.
Dislocation motion is a structural mediator of the proposed intervention's effect.
Machine-learning models can efficiently explore the vast compositional space of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning models can accurately predict high-entropy-alloy thermodynamic properties.
Traditional experimental and computational methods have limited accuracy, availability, and efficiency for the target properties.
The intervention will improve the accuracy of melting-temperature determination relative to traditional experimental and computational methods.
The intervention will improve determination of enthalpy and entropy of fusion relative to traditional methods.
The intervention will improve determination of volume change upon melting relative to traditional methods.
The intervention will improve determination of liquid thermodynamic properties relative to traditional methods.
The intervention will increase the availability and efficiency of predictions across a large compositional space.
The hypothesis is limited to unspecified high-entropy-alloy composition ranges and temperature conditions.
Model accuracy may depend on the quality and quantity of training data.
The models may fail to capture some complex interactions and phenomena in high-entropy alloys.

The hypothesis would be falsified if machine-learning models showed no significant improvement in accuracy and efficiency over traditional methods when compared on alloys of varying composition and temperature.
